name: Indian Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Sinha, Samar. 2018. Indian Sign Language: A Linguistic Analysis of Its Grammar. Washington, DC: Gallaudet University Press. 227 pp. (Glottolog 577293, grammar)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Only the publisher's TOC and the Chapter 1 excerpt are open. TOC: ch. 2 'The Sublexical Structure of ISL' pp. 20-80 (publisher blurb: sign formation parameters, syllable structure, sonority hierarchy). The excerpt (ch. 1, Introduction) contains no statement on stress, prosody or accent; ch. 2 is paywalled (JSTOR j.ctv2rcnfqg.7).

sources.citation: Varanasi, Sinha and Dasgupta. 2025. Cross-Linguistic Phonological Similarity Analysis in Sign Languages Using HamNoSys. Proceedings of the Workshop on Sign Language Processing (ACL). DOI 10.18653/v1/2025.wslp-main.9
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Computational comparison of handshape/location/movement notations; the only hit for 'prosod' is the reference to Brentari 1998. No statement on ISL stress.

sources.citation: Zeshan, Ulrike. 2003. Indo-Pakistani Sign Language Grammar: A Typological Outline. Sign Language Studies 3(2): 157-212
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: Typological outline of IPSL; abstract mentions no phonology, so low probability of a stress statement, but it is the standard sketch and would settle whether prosody is treated at all.

sources.citation: Sinha, Samar. 2012. A Grammar of Indian Sign Language. PhD thesis, Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.citation: Zeshan, Ulrike. 2000. Sign Language in Indo-Pakistan: A Description of a Signed Language. Amsterdam: John Benjamins. Chapter 2, The Signs, pp. 17-54
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number HV2469.I53 Z47 2000); ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number HV2469.I53 Z47 2000
sources.note: First comprehensive description of IPSL; ch. 2 is the sublexical/phonological chapter (handshapes, movement patterns, nonmanual signals). Vasishta's review calls the phonological analysis preliminary, so a stress statement is possible but not likely. Harvard holds print (Widener Library (offsite storage) HV2469.I53 Z47 2000, (a scan can be requested through your own library); Google Books limited preview exists (id TY-dmc1h5OQC).

sources.note: First-page excerpt (Internet Archive copy of Project MUSE page): 'Zeshan summarizes her preliminary research on handshapes used in IPSL. She believes the data were insufficient for a detailed phonological analysis. Her study shows that there are ten basic handshapes in IPSL' (p. 343). Nothing on stress.
